problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}11 & -8 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & a \\ 1 & b\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ find the value of $a-2b.$
worked_solution:
From the Jordan matrix $J,$ we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=7.
$$

As a result, we obtain that 

- the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ of the eigenvalue $\lambda =3,$

- the second column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{2}$ such that $(A-7I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}.$

Now, computing $A-7I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-7I & =[\begin{aligned}11 & -8 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]-(7)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the matrix equation $(A-7I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get  

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a-2b=\frac{5}{2}-2\cdot 1=\frac{1}{2}.$
